name: EDELWEISS
notes: INSPIRE lists EDELWEISS, EDELWEISS-II (recid 1108221) and EDELWEISS-III (recid 1298911) as separate experiment records, none carrying populated proposal/approval/start/completion dates; all generations are represented as one experiment:edelweiss record per the convention used elsewhere in this file. external.inspire_experiment cites the base recid (1110596).

No official EDELWEISS website could be reached (checked 2026-10-25: edelweiss.in2p3.fr and www.edelweiss.in2p3.fr do not resolve); all sourcing for this record comes from arXiv papers and the INSPIRE registry.

Early history (founding date, EDELWEISS-I/II/III transition dates, detector generations before the current 200 g NbSi-TES programme) is not recorded: no source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) states them. A working official site or a detector-history paper would settle this.

physics_goals.quote: The EDELWEISS collaboration reports on the search for Dark Matter (DM) particle interactions via Migdal effect ... using a 200 g cryogenic Ge detector sensitive to simultaneously heat and ionization signals
value: Search for sub-GeV dark matter via the Migdal effect and ionization/phonon signals in germanium bolometers

summary.plain: EDELWEISS searches for dark matter using pure germanium crystals cooled to near absolute zero, deep under a mountain in the French Alps. Recent versions are sensitive enough to look for dark matter far lighter than a proton.
summary.technical: Cryogenic germanium bolometer dark matter search at the Laboratoire Souterrain de Modane; the current sub-GeV programme uses a 200 g Ge detector with an NbSi transition-edge sensor and Neganov-Trofimov-Luke phonon amplification, reaching a 4.46 eV electron-recoil resolution and a 30 eV analysis threshold, searching for WIMPs down to 32 MeV/c² via the Migdal effect (2022-2024 results); a follow-on 'CRYOSEL' detector design is under development. Earlier EDELWEISS, EDELWEISS-II and EDELWEISS-III generations are not documented in detail here because no official EDELWEISS site could be reached (checked 2026-10-25).

unique_capabilities.quote: a RMS resolution of 4.46 electron-hole pairs was obtained on a massive (200g) germanium detector instrumented with a NbSi Transition Edge Sensor (TES)
value: Germanium bolometers with simultaneous heat and ionization readout; NbSi TES with Neganov-Trofimov-Luke phonon amplification for sub-GeV sensitivity
